document.title: A practical loop for small experiments
document.summary: Small experiments become useful when each one starts with a clear question and ends with recorded evidence.
document.author: Repurposer Example Team

sections.heading: Choose one question
paragraphs: Write down the single uncertainty that matters most to the next decision.
A narrow question makes the result easier to interpret and share.
bullets: Set a review date before work begins.

sections.heading: Collect visible evidence
paragraphs: Save the observed result beside the question so another person can inspect it.
Record failed attempts because they narrow the available choices.
bullets: Link each conclusion to an observation.

sections.heading: Decide the next move
paragraphs: Compare the evidence with the original question and choose a concrete follow-up.
Close the experiment when the decision has enough support.
bullets: Stop when the evidence answers the question.
